# ADR Basics 2: Creating a System-level ADR

# System-level ADR Process

Each system-level ADR is formatted the same way, and goes through the same workflow process. Our process strives for:

* **Transparency** \- ADRs are recorded in Confluence in a central location where access is fairly open.  
* **Approval** \- ADRs are approved by technology leaders to ensure they fit with an overall tech mission.  
* **Community Involvement** \- A review period is included to ensure that the technology community has ample time for comment and discussion.  
* **Evangelism** \- The architecture team utilizes the \#staff-engineering channel to post about new and approved ADRs.  
* **Actionable Results** \- Each ADR contains a section to describe actionable tasks that need to be done once an ADR is accepted.  
* **Visibility** \- Each ADR is tagged using labels and includes a section with other approved ADRs with the same label.

This is the workflow that each ADR goes through:

# Filling out an ADR

## Title and Labels

The title of your ADR should be descriptive as to the topic it addresses. ADRs do not get a number assigned until they are approved, so you do not need to worry about that when you are creating your ADR.

Labels are used to help classify ADRs. Add one or more label to your ADR page that associates it with a topic. 

## Header and Page Properties

In the Page Properties section, you will see a table with critical information in it. Use this guide to fill out the appropriate ADR.

| Label | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- |
| Record | Numeric marker for the ADR. Until approved, this section is blank, |
| Status | Status of the ADR. Can be **DRAFT**, **IN REVIEW**, **APPROVED** or **DEPRECATED.** |
| Topic | Title of your ADR. Short description of what the point of the ADR is. |
| Owner | Tagged with the @, the person or persons responsible for the ADR. |
| Requestor | Tagged with the @, the person or persons who requested the ADR. Can be a team as well. |
| Request Date | The date that you started working on the ADR. |
| Decision | Short text of the decision of the ADR. |
| Decision Date | Date that the decision was approved. This will be filled in after the ADR is approved by all parties and should stay blank until then. |
| Sign-off By | By Checkbox list stating all reviewers, tagged with the @. These should be leaders who the ADR affects or have influence over the topic discussed. |

## ADR Content

We use [Y-Statements](https://medium.com/olzzio/y-statements-10eb07b5a177) to record our choices, which gives a simple, story-like record of our decision.

*In the context of **\< some medium \>**,*  
*Facing the need **\< requirement faced \>**,*  
*We decided **\< decision made \>**,*  
*And against **\< alternatives discussed \>**,*  
*To achieve the ability **\< what you have enabled \>**,*  
*Accepting that **\< concessions and assumptions made \>**.*

## Additional Resources

This is a bulleted list of documents or links that back up the ADR. If you have documents such as diagrams or Google Docs, export those to a static file format and attach it to the ADR. 

## Related ADRs

Links to additional related documents that are similar to the ADR at hand.

## Post-Acceptance Action Items

This is a list of any actionable tasks that need to be done once an ADR is accepted. Some examples include:

- Clarifying language in other ADRs  
- Deprecating an existing ADR  
- Creating tickets in JIRA to satisfy compliance with this ADR  
- Updating documentation to denote the architectural change  
- Ideally, these items will have owners tagged (tagged with an @ in Google/Confluence).

# Ready for Review

Before you send your ADR for review, remember a few tips:

- Make sure your ADR is focused on how the decision affects the architecture. While timing and deadlines may affect the need to make the decision now, it should not be included in the ADR as a reason that the specific decision was made.  
- Use plain, simple, easy-to-understand language in your ADR.   
- Ensure any additional resources that could help reviewers are available and attached to the ADR.  
- Validate spelling, grammar, and formatting are correct.

Once you are happy with your ADR, notify Architecture.

# During The Review Process

- Be responsive to comments left in Confluence on your ADR.  
- Feel free to refine the content based on community and reviewer feedback.

# Post-Acceptance

Once all reviewers have signed off on the ADR, it is important that the post-acceptance tasks are followed up on. Those tasks are the responsibility of the owner of the ADR, but Architecture will follow up in case the owner needs assistance.

# Deprecating an ADR

As architecture changes, ADRs can become obsolete and no longer applicable. When this happens, notify Architecture and we can move an ADR to a **DEPRECATED** status. Typically, ADRs are deprecated and replaced by another ADR.
